summary: Relates to the residence of sex offender registrants.
title: Relates to the residence and domicile of sex offender registrants

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 229

TO THE ASSEMBLY:

I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:

Assembly Bill Number 1819-A, entitled:

    "AN ACT to amend the correction law, in relation to the sex offender
      registry"

    NOT APPROVED

  Since  its inception, law enforcement has interpreted the Sex Offender
Registration Act (SORA) to require  a  sex  offender  to  register  each
address  at  which he or she lives. This legislation would amend SORA to
define the term "residence" as any place where a sex offender  maintains
a  fixed,  permanent  home  to  which  he or she, when temporarily away,
intends to return.

  While I fully support the goal of  creating  a  definition  of  "resi-
dence",  this  proposal  creates significant public safety concerns. The
bill would effectively allow sex  offenders  to  avoid  registration  by
living  continuously  in  a temporary residence or shelter. For example,
some sex offenders stay in hotels or with friends  or  relatives.  Other
sex offenders may be homeless, and frequently move from shelter to shel-
ter.    Because none of those "residences" are "fixed" or "permanent" as
defined in the bill, they would not be captured by the bill.

  Despite  my  efforts  to  negotiate  an  amendment  to  address  these
concerns,  we  were  unable  to  reach a resolution with the Legislature
before delivery of the bill. I am therefore  constrained  to  veto  this
bill.    However,  I  am  directing  the  Department of Criminal Justice
Services to work with the bill's sponsors and interested stakeholders to
consider an amendment that would define residence in a  more  comprehen-
sive manner.

  The bill is disapproved.                    (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO

                               __________
